FigS1: Field temperature during day and night under the three sunlight treatments. Boxplots summarize the recorded distributions.
FigS2: Field temperature through time under the three sunlight treatments, shown separately for day and night.
FigS3: Field relative humidity during day and night under the three sunlight treatments.
FigS4: Field relative humidity through time under the three sunlight treatments, shown separately for day and night.
FigS5: Dominant fungal and bacterial genus-level categories in field litter. Each stacked bar represents one sample and sums to 100%. The twelve most abundant categories per marker are shown, with remaining categories grouped as Other. Unclassified labels retain their available family assignment. The prevalence filter requires detection in at least two samples before rarefaction.
FigS6: Field genus-level differential abundance for fungi and bacteria across the three pairwise sunlight contrasts. All eligible genera with at least ten counts across retained samples are tested using DESeq2 with fixed blocking terms. Points show log2 fold changes and BH-adjusted p-values. Labels identify significant categories.
FigS7: Relative representation of the targeted functional groups in field litter. Points represent samples; boxes show medians and interquartile ranges. Facet q-values are BH-adjusted omnibus sunlight-treatment tests across the thirteen variable groups. Models include the field replicate as a fixed blocking term.
FigS8: Microcosm fungal and bacterial genus composition. Each stacked bar represents one sample. Samples are grouped by substrate sunlight treatment and ordered by inoculum origin within each substrate, then by block and sample ID. Tick labels give sample ID and inoculum treatment. Colors identify genus-level categories consistently within each marker; remaining categories are grouped as Other.
FigS9: Comparison of field and microcosm litter microbiomes. Upper panels show the union of the ten most abundant genus-level categories in each experiment, using equal sample weights and all retained ASV reads before rarefaction. Unresolved assignments are retained as explicit categories. Lower panels show shared and experiment-specific detected named genus labels, excluding unresolved assignments. Circle areas are not proportional to counts; non-detection does not establish ecological exclusivity. This comparison is descriptive.
FigS10: Microcosm genus-level differential abundance among substrate treatments. The DESeq2 analysis estimates common substrate differences while accounting for fixed inoculum-by-block nuisance terms. It does not include a substrate-by-inoculum interaction and is distinct from the factorial community PERMANOVA. Fold changes and adjusted p-values retain the existing genus-level analysis.
FigS11: Relative abundances of twelve variable targeted functional groups in the microcosms. Colors identify substrate treatment and shapes identify inoculum origin. Faint points are individual samples; large points and error bars are model-estimated inoculum-by-substrate cell means and pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Models include fixed inoculum, substrate, and interaction effects with random block. Displayed F and p values are Type III Satterthwaite tests; q-values use BH correction across twelve groups separately for each term. Relative abundance is expressed as a percentage of the complete KO profile. N = 41. The all-zero lignin-associated oxidation group is excluded.
